title: Border-aware routing policy & customer access matrix for EU data residency
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a border-aware routing policy that enforces EU-only data residency constraints while supporting tier routing (hosted, dedicated, private) and automated fallback to pre-approved model variants. Deliver a tenant-level allowlist/denylist enforcement matrix, audit logs for routing decisions, and a policy engine that can be evaluated by compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy can be defined per-tenant as: EU-only, region-preferred, or global
Tenant-level allowlist and denylist influence routing decisions and are honored across hosted/dedicated/private runtimes
Fallback model mapping returns pre-approved EU-hosted model variants when primary route is unavailable without leaking non-EU compute
All routing decisions produce audit logs with policy id, evaluated rules, selected region, selected model variant, and reason for fallback
Automated test harness that simulates region failures and verifies tenant constraints remain satisfied
Console shows per-tenant routing summary and exposes a per-route 'compliance-safe' toggle
tasks: Spec: policy DSL extension for 'border-aware' rules and tenant access matrix (ENG)
Schema: add tenant.allowlist and tenant.denylist to control-plane datastore (ENG)
Runtime: routing decision hook to evaluate policy against request metadata and available capacity (ENG)
Models: maintain model-variant metadata with 'region-compatibility' tags (ENG/Research)
Audit: wire decision logger to event pipeline and retention policy (ENG/Observability)
Console: add tenant compliance page and manual override per-route (Product/Frontend)
E2E tests: simulate EU-region outage and validate fallback behavior (QA)
Security review: KMS/HSM data residency checks for private deployments (Security)
updates: 2025-02-20 - Created ticket. Initial scoping with PM and Legal. Identified need for tenant allowlist/denylist matrix rather than global switches to support resellers.

2025-02-24 - Architecture sync: decided on two-layer evaluation: 1) policy-level (tenant flags + geo constraints) 2) runtime capability filter (available capacity and model flags). Liam to draft policy DSL example by 02/28.

2025-03-01 - Prototype: implemented policy evaluator stub in routing module (branch: feat/border-aware-routing). Basic unit tests pass for static mappings. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/431

2025-03-03 - Legal review: confirmed EU-only must prevent routing to any non-EU compute for both inference and ephemeral caching. Raised KMS residency question for Private deployments. Added Security as collaborator.
2025-03-05 - Design review with Console team: agreed on 'compliance-safe' toggle UX and that manual overrides require audit justification. Next: schema changes and migration plan.
ToDo: Add telemetry histogram for 'policy-eval-latency' to ensure routing cost doesn't exceed SLOs (owner: Observability).
decision_rationale: We selected a tenant-first allowlist/denylist model so customers with mixed residency requirements (e.g., EU customers and non-EU customers under same org) can be handled without brittle global flags. Two-layer evaluation (policy -> capability) lets the control plane reason about compliance separately from transient capacity constraints and simplifies audit trails.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary) - Enable for internal test tenants only; evaluate over 48h under simulated EU outage
Phase 2 (beta) - Opt-in for select customers with strict residency needs; monitor errors and latency for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (ga) - Default enforcement for tenants with 'EU-only' flag; provide migration tooling and tenant report
Rollback - Feature flag to disable border-aware enforcement; automatic revert if >1% compliance-violation errors
risks: Latency: extra policy evaluation and model-variant lookup could add ~2-5ms per request; needs benchmarking
Capacity churn: strict EU-only constraints may increase contention in EU pools and cause higher cost/denied requests
Operator error: manual overrides in Console could accidentally bypass residency rules if not gated
Incomplete metadata: legacy model variants missing 'region-compatibility' tags could cause incorrect fallbacks
test_plan: Unit tests for policy DSL parsing and evaluation rules
Integration tests that register synthetic tenants and simulate multi-region compute availability
Chaos tests: kill EU capacity nodes and verify automated fallback does not route to non-EU compute for EU-only tenants
Compliance audit test that replays logs for a request and validates the stored decision trail matches expected rules
notes: Implementation must be backwards-compatible with existing routing policies; default behavior remains unchanged unless tenant flag set.
Consider a temporary quota bump path for EU-only tenants to reduce failure rate during capacity pressure (follow-up with Capacity Planning).
Follow-up ticket required to add rate-limited re-routing telemetry so we can quantify cost delta after GA.
Avoid embedding tenant-sensitive policy logic in edge proxies; evaluation should occur in control-plane/routing service to centralize auditability.
